messages.content: tell a story about a woman finding a photo in a book and choosing to send it to her sister.

a woman opened a book she had not read for a long time. inside was a photo of her and her sister by the garden wall. she took it out and put it on the table. in the photo, both were little, and each had a book in one hand. the woman could remember the morning when their father made the photo. they had been waiting for him to finish work so he could read with them. she chose to write to her sister about that day. after writing a short letter, she put the photo with it. she kept the book on the table so she could start reading again after she sent the letter. now the photo could give her sister a way to remember the same morning.
did she leave the photo in the book?
no. she put it with a letter to her sister.
who had made the photo in the story?
their father.
why did she keep the book on the table?
so she could start reading it again after she sent the letter.
write a story about two friends making a plan for a quiet afternoon. one asks about where to go and what to bring.

two friends had a free afternoon and would like to spend it together. one said they could go outside, but the other asked where they would go. they talked about the park, then chose the little garden behind the house because it was near. next, one asked if they should bring food. they had already had lunch, so they chose just water and two apples. one friend brought a book, and the other brought paper to draw on. when they got to the garden, they sat at the table under the tree. there was no need to do the same thing all the time. they read and drew for a while, then ate the apples and talked. asking each other about the afternoon had helped them make a simple plan they could both enjoy.
did they go to the park?
no. they chose the garden behind the house.
why did they not bring a large lunch?
they had already had lunch.
did both friends read?
no. one brought a book, and the other brought paper for drawing.
tell a story about a child hearing a voice and finding out which person in the family is talking.

a child was drawing in the bedroom when he could hear a voice in the kitchen. it was like the voice of his uncle, but he was not sure. he put his pencil down and went to the door. his mother was on the phone, and the voice was coming from it. his uncle was not in the house. the child waited while his mother finished talking, then asked if he could say hello. she called his uncle again for a short talk. the child said he did not know his uncle was talking on the phone instead of visiting. his uncle said he would like to visit another day, but today he was at his own home. after the call, the child went back to his picture. now he drew a phone on the table next to the house.
was his uncle in the kitchen?
no. the voice came from the phone.
where was the uncle?
at his own home.
did the child get to talk to him?
yes. his mother called again so he could say hello.
write a story about a girl saying she will return a book and doing it even before her friend asks.

a girl had a book from her friend. she said she would bring it back the next day because her friend would need it for school. that evening, she read the last page she had time for, then put a little note inside so she could remember the place. she was not finished, but she knew the book had to go back. in the morning, she put it in her bag before breakfast. at school, she found her friend by the door and gave her the book. her friend said thank you and asked if it was a good story. the girl said she would like to finish it another time. her friend said she could have it again after the school work was done. both were happy they could share the same book.
did the girl wait for her friend to ask for it?
no. she brought it back the next day as she had said she would.
had she finished reading it?
no. she would like to finish another time.
could she read it again later?
yes. her friend said she could have it again after the school work was done.
tell a story about someone trying to carry too many things and asking for help.

a man came from the shop with a bag of food, a box, and a book under his arm. when he got to his house, he could not get the key from his coat while holding everything. he tried to put the book on top of the box, but it would not stay there. his neighbor was walking by and asked if he would like help. at first he said he could do it, then looked at the things in his arms and changed his mind. he asked her to hold the book while he put the box down. with one hand free, he found the key and opened the door. she gave the book back, and he said thank you. he did not have to carry everything at once to get it home.
what did the neighbor hold?
the book.
did she take the key and open the door for him?
no. he found the key and opened the door with a free hand.
why did he change his mind about help?
he could not get the key while holding everything.
write a story about a boy who is worried that his little drawing is not enough to give his grandmother.

a boy made a drawing for his grandmother. it was a picture of the kitchen table where they often sat together. he put two cups, a book, and the window behind the table in the picture. when he finished, he looked at it and said it was only a piece of paper. his father asked what the picture was about. the boy said it was about having tea and reading with his grandmother. his father said he could tell her that when he gave it to her. at the visit, the boy held out the picture and said he had made it to show a place he could enjoy with her. his grandmother put it on the table next to their cups. she asked him to tell her about each part. they talked for a long time, and the little piece of paper was part of their visit.
what was in the picture the boy made?
the kitchen table where he and his grandmother often sat together.
did she ask him to bring a large thing instead?
no. she asked him to tell her about the picture.
why was the picture about a good time for him?
it was about a place he could enjoy and time he had with his grandmother.
tell a story about a girl asking to play, not hearing an answer, and then finding out why.

a girl stood by the kitchen door and asked her brother if he would like to play outside. he did not answer. she started to walk away, thinking he did not want to play. then she saw that he was looking at the open book in front of him. she went over and said his name. he looked up and asked what she had said. she asked again, and he said he would like to play after finishing the page. he had not been listening the first time. the girl sat down with paper while she waited. when he closed the book, they put their things away and went to the garden. not hearing an answer had not been the same as hearing no.
did the brother say no to the first question?
no. he had not been listening the first time.
what did he want to finish before playing?
the page he was reading.
what did the girl do while she waited?
she sat down with paper.
write a story about a person who often cannot find a small key and chooses one place for it.

a woman often put a small key down while doing other things. one day it was on the kitchen table, and another day it was under a book. she could find it, but looking took time. one evening, she chose a little box on the shelf by the door. she put the key inside and said she would try keeping it there. the next morning, she opened the box before going out, and the key was ready. when she came home, she put it back before taking off her coat. after that, she still had to remember to use the box. the box did not move the key on its own. it just gave her one place to choose each time she put it away.
did the key always go into the box on its own?
no. she had to remember to put it there.
where was the box?
on the shelf by the door.
what did she do when she came home?
she put the key back before taking off her coat.
tell a story about two people getting a room ready for a visit. they do not have to do the same work.

a brother and sister were getting the living room ready before their aunt came. the boy put books on the shelf while the girl cleaned the little table. when he finished, he went to the kitchen to get cups. she moved a chair by the window so their aunt could sit where there was light. then the boy brought water, and the girl found a clean towel for the bathroom. both looked around the room before the visit. the books were ready, the table was clean, and there was a place to sit. they had not done the same thing, but both had helped. when their aunt came, they asked her about her day instead of talking only about the work they had done.
who cleaned the table?
the girl.
did the boy help too?
yes. he put books on the shelf and brought cups and water.
why did they move a chair by the window?
so their aunt could sit where there was light.
write a story about a person who is asked to play a game but would like to just sit with a friend instead.

a woman went to visit her friend, who had put a game on the table. her friend asked if she would like to play. the woman said she was tired and would like to sit and talk instead. her friend put the game on the shelf and brought two cups of water. they sat near the window, and the woman talked about her work. after a while, she asked about the book her friend had been reading. they looked at the first page together. the game was still on the shelf at the end of the visit. they did not need to play it to enjoy being together. before going home, the woman said thank you for a quiet afternoon.
did she say she did not like her friend?
no. she was tired and would like quiet time together instead of a game.
where did the game go?
on the shelf.
did they play it before she left?
no. it was still on the shelf at the end of the visit.
tell a story about a child finding a thing in a kitchen and asking what it is. use a simple kitchen thing.

a child stood next to his father while he got dinner ready. on the table were a spoon, a fork, and a little bowl. the child took the fork and asked why it was not a spoon. his father put some soup in the spoon, then put a piece of food on the fork. the child asked if he could use the spoon for everything. his father said he could try, but some food might be easy to eat with a fork. at dinner, the child took the spoon for soup and then tried the fork with a little piece of carrot. he did not have to know everything at once. asking one question had helped him learn about the things in front of him.
what did the child ask about?
the fork and why it was not a spoon.
what did he use for soup?
the spoon.
did his father say he had to know everything right away?
no. the story says he could learn by asking one question at a time.
write a story about a girl who would like to help her brother but has one line of work to finish first.

a girl was writing at the table when her brother asked if she could help him find his shoes. she said she could help after finishing the line she was on. her brother sat by the door and waited. she wrote the last word, put the pen in its box, and came over. first they looked under the sofa, where they found one shoe. then she asked where he had put the other one after taking it off. he could remember sitting on his bed before lunch. they went to the bedroom, and the shoe was by the bed under a shirt. he put both shoes on and said thank you. she went back to the table, where her paper was still ready for her next line.
did she leave her writing before finishing the line?
no. she finished the line first, then helped.
where was the first shoe?
under the sofa.
where did they find the other one?
by the bed under a shirt.
tell a story about a woman making a note before a phone call so she can remember what to ask.

a woman would like to call her brother about a family visit. she had two things to ask: which day he could come and if he would bring his children. before calling, she took a small piece of paper and wrote both things down. during the call, they first talked about work and the weather. then she looked at the note and asked about the visit. he said he could come tomorrow and would bring both children. she wrote tomorrow under the first line and two children under the next. after the call, she left the note on the kitchen table. now she could tell her family what he had said about the visit, even with the talk about work still on her mind.
did the note answer the question for her?
no. it helped her remember what to ask during the call.
when was her brother coming?
tomorrow.
was he coming alone?
no. he said he would bring both children.
write a story about a boy reading a story and then going back to understand one part.

a boy was reading a story about a child who left a book at school. he read one page and said the child had lost the book at the park. his sister asked him to look at the page again. this time, he took his time with each line. the story said the child went to the park after school, but the book was still on the desk at school. the boy had put the place of the walk together with the place of the book. he went back to the first line and read it to his sister. now he could say where the book was. they kept reading and found that the child would get it back the next morning.
was the book at the park?
no. it was still on the desk at school.
what helped the boy understand?
he went back and read the page again, taking his time.
did he need to make up a new part of the story?
no. he found the answer in the words already on the page.
tell a quiet story about someone sitting in a garden. they do not need to work or make a plan.

a man took a chair into the garden and put it by the wall. he had brought a book, but he left it closed on the little wall. for a while, he just looked at the tree. the wind moved a leaf, and a bird came down by the wall before going back up. from the kitchen, he could hear a little music on the radio. there were things he could have cleaned or moved, but he could choose to rest instead. he sat and had some water, then opened the book when he felt like reading. after one page, he looked up again. the garden was still there, and he did not have to work in it to enjoy it.
did he start cleaning the garden?
no. he sat, had water, and read a page when he felt like it.
was the book open from the start?
no. he left it closed for a while.
where did the music come from?
the radio in the kitchen.
write a story about someone seeing a small thing from a window and not knowing what it is at first.

a child looked out of the kitchen window and saw a little red shape by the garden wall. he asked his mother if it was a ball. she looked too and said it might be, but they were not near enough to be sure. they went outside to look. by the wall was a red hat that his sister had left there after playing. the child took it and brought it inside. his mother asked if it had been a ball after all. he said no, it only looked like one from the window. they put the hat by the door so his sister could find it. the child was happy they had looked instead of saying for sure while they were still inside.
what was the red thing?
it was the hat his sister left outside.
did they know that from the window?
no. they went outside to look before knowing for sure.
where did they put it?
by the door so his sister could find it.
tell a story about a person saying they do not understand a game and asking to try one step.

a woman sat at a table with two friends who knew a game she had never played. they started telling her what to do, but there were many things to remember. she said she did not understand and asked if they could try one step first. one friend put a card on the table and asked her to choose a card from her hand. they played that part once, then tried the next part. after a short time, she could follow what was happening. she still asked a question now and then, and her friends answered. by the end, she could start a game on her own. saying she did not understand had helped all of them know where to begin.
did she say she knew the game even when she did not?
no. she said she did not understand and asked to try one step.
what did her friend put on the table?
a card.
did she stop asking once the game started?
no. she still asked when she had a question.
write a story about making space for one more person at a table.

a family was having lunch when an uncle came to visit. there were three chairs at the table, and all three had someone sitting on them. the daughter got up and went to the bedroom for a little chair. her brother moved his plate so there would be room for another one. their mother brought a cup from the kitchen and asked if the uncle would like some food. he said he had already had lunch, but would enjoy sitting with them and having water. the daughter put the chair by the end of the table, then sat down again in her own place. now all four could talk together. they did not need a new table, just a little room and another chair.
how many chairs were there at first?
three.
did the uncle need a large meal?
no. he had already had lunch and asked to sit with them and have water.
who got another chair?
the daughter got it from the bedroom.
tell a story about someone trying two pens before choosing which to use for a letter.

a man sat down to write a letter with two pens on the table. one was black, and the other was blue. he chose the blue one first because he would like that color for the letter. after writing a few words, he found it hard to hold. he put it down and tried the black pen on another piece of paper. that one felt easy in his hand. he could still enjoy blue, but the letter would take time to write. he chose the black pen and put the blue one back in the box. when he finished, he read the letter to make sure the words were easy to follow. then he put the black pen in the same place so he could find it next time.
did he choose only by color in the end?
no. he chose the pen that felt easy to hold.
which pen did he use for the letter?
the black pen.
did he say he could not enjoy blue now?
no. he could still enjoy blue and choose the black pen for writing.
write a story about a child learning one thing about a parent and asking to talk more another day.

a child saw a little boat on a shelf in the bedroom of his mother. he asked if it had always been there. she took it down and said she had made it with her father when she was little. the child did not know she could build things. she said she had learned a little by trying with someone who could help. he asked how long it took to make, but she said she could not remember that part. they looked at the shape and the small place inside where a person would sit if the boat was large enough. before it went back on the shelf, the child asked if they could make a little boat together one day. she said they could talk about it again tomorrow.
who had helped his mother make the boat?
her father.
did she know everything about it?
no. she could not remember how long it took to make.
did they start building a boat right away?
no. they chose to talk about it again tomorrow.
